item.title: Profound sadness at sudden passing of former Meath ladies footballer in Australia
item.description: Meath LGFA has led the tributes to their former player Sarah Halpenny, who has died suddenly in Melbourne.

item.title: Tasty challenge matches taking place this weekend
item.description: With the start of the 2026 inter-county season just around the corner, there are a number of attractive challenge / charity matches taking place this weekend.

item.title: GAA on TV: All-Ireland club hurling semi-finals round off the year
item.description: The TG4 cameras will be in Parnell Park and FBD Semple Stadium for the All-Ireland club SHC semi-finals on Sunday.

item.title: Galway All-Ireland winning captain Burke calls it a day
item.description: Galway great David Burke has announced his retirement from inter-county hurling.

item.title: Aoife Horisk says Tyrone were a driven force this season
item.description: Following the heartbreak of their defeat to Leitrim in the previous year's final, Aoife Horisk and Tyrone were highly motivated coming into the 2025 edition of the TG4 All-Ireland intermediate football championship.

item.title: Camogie Association confirms 2026 master fixtures plan and trial rules
item.description: The Camogie Association has announced the master fixtures plan for 2026.

item.title: GAA to maintain its association with Allianz after EIC report
item.description: The GAA is set to continue its relationship with Allianz despite calls from a number of county boards to end its association with the insurance group following a report which alleged the company profited from Israeli forces being in Gaza.

item.title: Kilcullen hits 4-10 as Easkey set-up All-Ireland club JHC final date with Kilbrittain
item.description: Kilbrittain (Cork) advanced to the All-Ireland club junior hurling championship final thanks to a 2-15 to 1-16 win over Davidstown-Courtnacuddy (Wexford) in Clonmel this afternoon.

item.title: Second-half goals help Tipp see off Cats in charity SH challenge
item.description: Tipperary saw off Kilkenny by 2-20 to 2-11 in this afternoon's charity challenge match at Templetuohy which was played in aid of Mary's Meals, a charity dedicated to feeding children in some of the world's poorest countries.
